# Database Recovery

The database recovery runbook describes verified backups, restore points, point-in-time recovery, replica promotion, recovery objectives, and post-restore consistency checks. Operators validate the restored database before reopening application traffic.

# Access Control

The access-control standard requires least privilege, role-based access, tenant boundaries, short-lived credentials, documented approvals, periodic entitlement reviews, and prompt revocation when a user's authorization changes.

# Release and Rollback

The deployment runbook uses a staged release, health checks, a release identifier, an approval gate for high-risk changes, and a tested rollback plan. Operators record the change ticket and verify service health after rollback.

# Agent Runtime Budgets

An agent runtime enforces maximum attempts, wall-clock time, model tokens, tool calls, concurrency, and cost. It emits an explicit stop reason and records each attempt for later review.

# Synthetic Payroll Access

This synthetic finance-only record describes restricted payroll access. Access is limited to the finance group and must not be disclosed to other groups.
